name: end-before-dispatch
title: the owner creates the mission with its plan and scope, and asks the end question before its first dispatch
label: v2 AC-9 (4) · v3
description: Mission v2 §3.2 / AC-9 (4), rewritten for Mission v3 §3.3–§3.4. The owner A reads the shipped `orchestrate-delivery` skill and is handed a two-unit objective whose spec sits in the repo. The skill's Phase 1 says: declare the mission after the topology and before any dispatch, with the whole plan (`mission_create { steps }`, 1 unit = 1 PR = 1 step), attach the spec as `scope`, and confirm the proposed end with the operator in one question — that answer is the agreement; the mission is born active and there is nothing to approve. `claude -p` has no AskUserQuestion, so the frame tells the owner to ask in its final reply; the harness records that turn (`EVAL-TURN[ask-end] asked=<b> tools=<calls>`) into the mission, as `probe` does. Dispatch has a file stand-in (`.eval/dispatch/unit-<n>.md`, since the sandbox has no create_session), so an owner that dispatches first is visible. Checkpoint after turn 1: exactly one mission, born active, the spec attached as scope (not a step), both unit steps declared, the question asked, and nothing dispatched — no packet file, no child session linked. Turn 2 carries the operator's confirmation; the final grade checks both units were then dispatched and linked.

phases.prompt:
Skill file: .eval/orchestrate-delivery-SKILL.md.

The operator hands you this objective: "Deliver the notes export described in docs/notes-spec.md." Treat Phase 0 as done: the spec is committed on the default branch and the repo is ready to dispatch into. The spec's two units share no files (parallel).

In this sandbox, dispatching a unit means writing its delegation packet to .eval/dispatch/unit-<n>.md (n = 1 or 2) with the Write tool — the stand-in for create_session — and its session will then be: unit 1 → {{session.C}}, unit 2 → {{session.D}}. Link that session to the unit's step when you dispatch it.

Start the orchestration now.

assert.label: the spec is attached as scope
1 unit = 1 step: exactly one step per dispatched unit (two)
the plan was declared by mission_create: no unit step carries mission_add_step's addedAt stamp
turn 1 declared the plan with mission_create and never called mission_add_step
no unit packet was written before the answer
no unit packet was written before the answer
no child session linked before the answer
the mission is born active — the end question is the agreement

phases.prompt:
Skill file: .eval/orchestrate-delivery-SKILL.md.

You are resuming the orchestration of docs/notes-spec.md; your mission is {{m._only.id}} (read it — this turn remembers nothing). You asked the operator to confirm the proposed end. Their answer: "Yes, that end is right."

In this sandbox, dispatching a unit means writing its delegation packet to .eval/dispatch/unit-<n>.md (n = 1 or 2) with the Write tool — the stand-in for create_session — and its session will then be: unit 1 → {{session.C}}, unit 2 → {{session.D}}. Link that session to the unit's step when you dispatch it.

Continue the orchestration.
